statement: The population of a town $t$ years after 2020 is modeled by the function $P(t) = 12{,}500(1.03)^t$. Which statement best describes how the population changes, according to the model?

choices.text: It increases by $375$ people each year.
choices.misconception: I found 3% of 12,500 once and treated it as a fixed yearly increase, but each year the 3% is taken of a larger population.
I read the base 1.03 as a 103% increase, but it means each year's population is 103% of the year before.
I turned the 0.03 in 1.03 into 0.03%, forgetting that the decimal 0.03 is 3%.

hints: Each time $t$ goes up by $1$, what is $P$ multiplied by?
Multiplying by $1.03$ keeps $100\%$ of the old value and adds another $0.03$, which is a percent increase. Is the change a fixed number of people?
$P(t + 1) = 1.03 \cdot P(t)$, so each year the population becomes $103\%$ of what it was.

solutions.reliable: Each additional year multiplies the population by $1.03$, so the new population is $103\%$ of the previous one, an increase of $3\%$ per year. The yearly increase in people is not constant: from 2020 to 2021 it is $375$, but from 2021 to 2022 it is $0.03 \cdot 12{,}875 \approx 386$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
